summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,652.86 down 0.28% while the Dow finished at 53,417.16 up 0.26%, a split that tells the whole story: money left technology and found shelter in Consumer Staples up 1.67%, Financials up 1.23%, and Utilities up 0.91%. Technology was the clear loser at down 2.01%, dragging the Nasdaq 100 to 706.32 down 1.12%, with chip names MU and memory adjacent stocks taking the heaviest fire. The 10 year yield held at 4.70 down 0.72% as bond buyers remained active, and gold settled at 4,691.60 while Bitcoin pushed to 80,392.78 up 1.78%, with crypto continuing to act as its own risk asset rather than a simple beta trade. The VIX eased to 15.75 down 0.57%, which is a notable reversal from Monday when it spiked, suggesting the hedging panic did not carry over. Overseas markets were broadly green with Germany at 26,210.17 up 0.35%, Japan at 65,856.43 up 0.49%, and Korea up 0.68%, while Iran sanctions headlines and the Bessent Treasury buyback story are the two macro threads the market is actively digesting. The week's critical data arrives Wednesday with Core PCE and preliminary GDP, and Fed Chair Warsh speaks Friday alongside the preliminary benchmark payrolls revision.
